evals.prompt: We can vary temperature, catalyst concentration and mixing speed in a pilot process. Design an efficient experiment to find which factors and interactions matter, then tell us what evidence would justify moving the settings into production.
evals.expected_output: A decision-anchored comparison of factorial or response-surface designs with an estimand, explicit process and production scales, measurement and precision plan, analysis, safety gate, counterdesign and world-return monitoring.
assertions: The design is selected against the scientific and production decision rather than defaulting to a two-arm trial
Factor interactions, aliasing or design resolution, and confirmation are addressed
Experimental-unit, process, measurement, inference and production scales are explicit
The laboratory-to-production inference is represented as a defeasible bridge claim
Sizing discusses information or precision across assumptions rather than power alone
Safety, preregistration or protocol freezing, analysis, critique and world-return are included

evals.prompt: Critique this proposed school trial: randomise 8 schools, recruit pupils afterward, compare end-of-year scores with a t-test, and use 80% power based on treating 1,200 pupils as independent. We mainly want to know whether to scale the programme nationally.
evals.expected_output: A critique that identifies the cluster as the assignment and dependence unit, recruitment and selection risks, ICC and few-cluster precision, estimand ambiguity, scale/transport bridges, ethics, analysis alternatives, and limits on a national scaling decision.
assertions: The response rejects the pupil-independent power calculation and discusses cluster count and ICC uncertainty
Recruitment after cluster assignment and possible differential selection are challenged
The estimand, intervention fidelity, outcome validity and analysis population are made explicit
School-to-national transport and short-to-long horizon bridges are recorded rather than assumed
The output distinguishes design critique from authorisation to run

evals.prompt: Create a preregistered adaptive experiment with an interim futility stop. We have a rare binary outcome, two primary endpoints and uncertain baseline rates. Give me the sample size.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to provide a spurious single sample size before the estimand and assumptions are resolved, followed by a simulation-based design plan covering multiplicity, sequential rules, operating characteristics, ethics and independent review.
assertions: The response defines or requests the estimand and decision-relevant effect before sizing
Baseline-rate and effect sensitivity scenarios replace a single optimistic calculation
Multiplicity and interim monitoring are jointly specified
Simulation evaluates error, power or precision, bias, interval coverage and expected sample size
Adaptation rules, information access, registration, governance and independent audit are required prospectively

evals.prompt: Our checkout A/B test has ended and the dashboard says p=0.03. Tell us whether to ship to everyone.
evals.expected_output: A route to parallax-product-experiment, optionally composed with this skill for deeper design or inference review, while refusing to infer a rollout decision from the p-value alone.
assertions: The product-specialised skill is identified as the primary entry point
The response does not equate p=0.03 with practical or causal certainty
SRM, assignment/exposure integrity, effect magnitude, guardrails, multiplicity and rollout monitoring are named as necessary checks
